newsitem.title: USA: American meat packers hope for EU poultry accord.
newsitem.headline: American meat packers hope for EU poultry accord.

text.p: The American Meat Institute said Wednesday that it was "satisfied" with the last-minute agreement reached by U.S. and EU trade negotiators, but expressed disappointment that the pact did not cover poultry.

"We find it incomprehensible that processing techniques widely used in the United States and required by export customers throughout the world to ensure the production of safe and wholesome U.S. poultry are incompatible with current EU standards," said J.Patrick Boyle, president of the meat institute.
He said the agreement's provision requiring a scientific study to assess different kinds of food safety techniques was "critical" and should be carried out as quickly as possible.

"The U.S. industry's objective has been, and should continue to be, recognition of full equivalence between the U.S. and EU meat and poultry inspection systems," Boyle said in a statement. "We would expect that this agreement today represents a step towards ultimately achieving that goal of equivalency."
The American Meat Institute represents packers and processors of beef, pork, lamb and turkey products.
Earlier Wednesday, the U.S. agriculture department said it reached an accord to prevent a costly trade war with the EU, but the pact covered only meat inspections and not poultry.
